name: DefaultJobSchedulerBeginPass
trigger: After taking the submitted-candidate snapshot and passing the locked capacity check; before inspecting its first candidate.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerEndPass
trigger: After the final candidate; before schedule_job processes accumulated failed/blocked metadata.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerSkipBackoff
trigger: At the time_since_last_schedule < required_interval continue branch, with the saved candidate ID.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerBackoffElapsed
note: Deadline crossing; elapsed seconds must be >= Backoff(j); no normal retry counter bound.
trigger: When monotonic elapsed time first satisfies the recorded backoff for this candidate; emit an observational deadline crossing.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerExhausted
note: The exhausted-candidate metadata write succeeds in this slice.
trigger: After appending this candidate to blocked_jobs and updating its history; before continuing the scan.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerTryJob
note: Connected valid selected sites pass applicability checks. AttemptSlots is a finite fresh-token universe, not retry policy.
trigger: At _try_job entry after retry/capacity gates; capture local candidate ID and assign a fresh attempt alias before sending checks.

name: ServerEngineCheckClientResources
trigger: After enqueueing the batch of CHECK_RESOURCE requests and opening waiter slots; before the blocking wait.

name: CheckResourceProcessorReserve
trigger: Inside the RM lock, after popleft and reserved_resources[token] assignment; capture the deque, UUID, payload and TTL before unlock.

name: CheckResourceProcessorUnavailable
trigger: Inside the RM lock, after the unavailable decision and before returning the negative check result.

name: ServerEngineReceiveCheckOK

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].check = IF rpc[s][t].check = "waiting" THEN "ok" ELSE rpc[s][t].check]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the CheckOK reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: ServerEngineReceiveCheckNo

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].check = IF rpc[s][t].check = "waiting" THEN "no" ELSE rpc[s][t].check]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the CheckNo reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: AdminCheckTimeout
note: Actual RPC deadline crossing; commands already sent remain executable.
trigger: When the blocking Check RPC batch reaches its deadline, after closing remaining waiter slots; retain executing commands and any late replies.

name: ServerEngineReceiveDeployOK

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].deploy = IF rpc[s][t].deploy = "waiting" THEN "ok" ELSE rpc[s][t].deploy]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the DeployOK reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: ServerEngineReceiveDeployNo

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].deploy = IF rpc[s][t].deploy = "waiting" THEN "no" ELSE rpc[s][t].deploy]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the DeployNo reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: AdminDeployTimeout
note: Actual RPC deadline crossing; commands already sent remain executable.
trigger: When the blocking Deploy RPC batch reaches its deadline, after closing remaining waiter slots; retain executing commands and any late replies.

name: ServerEngineReceiveStartOK

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].start = IF rpc[s][t].start = "waiting" THEN "ok" ELSE rpc[s][t].start]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the StartOK reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: ServerEngineReceiveStartNo

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].start = IF rpc[s][t].start = "waiting" THEN "no" ELSE rpc[s][t].start]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the StartNo reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: AdminStartTimeout
note: Actual RPC deadline crossing; commands already sent remain executable.
trigger: When the blocking Start RPC batch reaches its deadline, after closing remaining waiter slots; retain executing commands and any late replies.

name: ServerEngineReceiveCancelAck

updates.rpc: [rpc EXCEPT ![s][t].cancel = IF rpc[s][t].cancel = "waiting" THEN "ok" ELSE rpc[s][t].cancel]

note: Closed waiters discard late replies; no mutation of another token or lifecycle status.
trigger: After the CancelAck reply is matched to its original waiter, or discarded because that waiter closed; before aggregate return.

name: AdminCancelTimeout
note: Actual RPC deadline crossing; commands already sent remain executable.
trigger: When the blocking Cancel RPC batch reaches its deadline, after closing remaining waiter slots; retain executing commands and any late replies.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerEvaluateResources

updates.scheduler: [scheduler EXCEPT !.pc = IF Policy(ReplySites(CurrentToken,"check","ok")) THEN "history" ELSE "cancelSend", !.result = IF Policy(ReplySites(CurrentToken,"check","ok")) THEN "scheduled" ELSE "no_resource"]

trigger: After inspecting all returned check results and computing dispatch/minimum/required-site decision; before cancellation or success return.

name: ServerEngineCancelClientResources

updates.rpc: [s \in Sites |-> [rpc[s] EXCEPT ![CurrentToken].cancel = IF s \in jobs[CurrentJob].dispatch THEN "waiting" ELSE @]]

trigger: After enqueueing cancellation requests for known positive tokens, before waiting for replies.

name: CancelResourceProcessorCancel
note: Only existing reservations are returned. Missing or already allocated tokens are a no-op.
trigger: Inside the RM lock after conditional token pop and appendleft, including the missing-token no-op branch.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerCancelReturned
note: Pinned implementation discards cancellation acknowledgements, including timeout/no reply.
trigger: After _send_admin_requests returns, before returning from cancel_client_resources; replies are discarded by the pinned caller.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerUpdateHistory

updates.scheduler: [scheduler EXCEPT !.count[CurrentJob] = @+1, !.history[CurrentJob] = Append(@,scheduler.result), !.cooldown[CurrentJob] = TRUE, !.pc = IF scheduler.result="scheduled" THEN "persistFailed" ELSE "scan", !.returnTo = IF scheduler.result="scheduled" THEN "checkSubmitted" ELSE "idle", !.failedPending = IF scheduler.result="scheduled" THEN @ ELSE @ \cup {CurrentJob}, !.candidates = IF scheduler.result="scheduled" THEN @ ELSE Tail(@)]

trigger: Immediately after count/history/time update in the local Job metadata, before returning success or appending to failed_jobs.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerAdmissionException
note: Known #5191 context: whole pass exits, no new cancellation/history; TTL remains.
trigger: At the whole-pass except after _try_job or post-admission processing raises, before returning through deferred metadata processing.

name: AutoCleanResourceManagerTick

updates.rm: [rm EXCEPT ![s].ttl = [t \in Tokens |-> IF rm[s].ttl[t]>0 THEN rm[s].ttl[t]-1 ELSE 0]]

note: One cleanup scan tick. Expired entries are drained under the same RM lock by FinishExpiry; other RM operations are disabled while an expired entry exists.
trigger: Inside _check_expired lock, after decrementing positive token TTLs and building the expired list, before popping any expired entry.

name: AutoCleanResourceManagerFinishExpiry
note: Internal lock-held scan continuation, not a release/reacquire window. Drain order over tokens overapproximates insertion order; unit conservation is order-independent.
trigger: Inside the same cleanup lock, immediately after one expired token pop and its _deallocate appendleft operations.

name: JobRunnerCheckSubmitted
note: Status read and subsequent DISPATCHED publication are separate.
trigger: At completion of the SUBMITTED status read/check; capture the actual read value before entering deployment or continuing.

name: JobRunnerDeployJob

updates.rpc: [s \in Sites |-> [rpc[s] EXCEPT ![CurrentToken].deploy = IF s \in jobs[CurrentJob].dispatch THEN "waiting" ELSE @]]

note: Server deployment succeeds here; DeploymentException models the raised/returned-error path.
trigger: After local server deployment succeeds and client DEPLOY batch is enqueued, before waiting on deployment replies.

name: JobRunnerDeploymentException
trigger: At the exception/returned-error branch in _deploy_job, before runner exception cleanup.

name: ClientDeploySuccess
note: Boundary abstraction of successful client deployment; no workspace content modeled.
trigger: After engine.deploy_app returns success and deployment has committed, at the successful reply boundary.

name: ClientDeployError
note: Client deployment returns non-OK; already successful sites remain deployed.
trigger: At the ordinary staging/deployment error reply boundary; retain state at other successful sites.

name: JobRunnerEvaluateDeployment
trigger: After building failed_clients and checking min_sites/required_sites, before _deploy_job returns or raises.

name: JobRunnerWriteDispatched
trigger: Immediately after persistent DISPATCHED update commits, before deployment-detail metadata update.

name: JobRunnerPersistDeploy
trigger: After deployment details/retry metadata update commits, before the DISPATCHED status check.

name: JobRunnerCheckDispatched
trigger: Immediately after the DISPATCHED read/check and before calling _start_run.

name: ServerEngineSpawnJob
note: Default local server spawn; physical exit remains a separate event.
trigger: Immediately at successful default local server spawn; retain handle/PID identity independently from run_processes.

name: ServerEngineRegisterJob
trigger: Inside server engine lock, immediately after run_processes[job_id] publication.

name: ServerEngineInstallWaiter
note: Server waiter thread creation succeeds in this slice; the targeted installation failure is client-side.
trigger: Immediately after the server wait_for_complete thread starts successfully.

name: JobRunnerSetPendingOutcomes
trigger: Inside runner lock, after assigning _pending_client_outcomes[job_id].

name: ServerEngineStartClientJob

updates.rpc: [s \in Sites |-> [rpc[s] EXCEPT ![CurrentToken].start = IF s \in jobs[CurrentJob].deployed THEN "waiting" ELSE @]]

trigger: After enqueueing exactly the deployable START_JOB batch with token/job headers; before its 20-second waiter.

name: JobRunnerEvaluateStartReplies

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![CurrentJob].active = IF ReplySites(CurrentToken,"start","no") # {} \/ jobs[CurrentJob].deployed = {} \/ (StrictStart /\ ~Policy(ReplySites(CurrentToken,"start","ok"))) THEN jobs[CurrentJob].deployed ELSE ReplySites(CurrentToken,"start","ok")]
updates.scheduler: [scheduler EXCEPT !.pc = IF ReplySites(CurrentToken,"start","no") # {} \/ jobs[CurrentJob].deployed = {} \/ (StrictStart /\ ~Policy(ReplySites(CurrentToken,"start","ok"))) THEN "failRemove" ELSE "filterOutcomes"]

note: check_client_replies and strict participant errors raise before filtering the initialized deployed-site list (runner:313-358).
trigger: After check_client_replies and active-client selection, before pending-outcome intersection; capture actual reply slots and strict policy.

name: JobRunnerFilterPendingOutcomes
trigger: Inside runner lock, after intersection_update(active_client_sites), before JOB_STARTED dispatch.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerJobStarted
note: Synchronous production event dispatch, explicit job ID, set-like idempotent membership; ordinary component exceptions do not propagate.
trigger: Inside scheduler.handle_event lock after idempotent scheduled_jobs insertion; retain EVENT_DATA job ID, before synchronous dispatch returns.

name: JobRunnerRegisterRunning
trigger: Inside runner lock, immediately after running_jobs[job_id] insertion and before set_status(RUNNING).

name: JobRunnerWriteRunning
note: No expected-state guard; terminalPublished is a history observer for this attempt.
trigger: Immediately after persistent RUNNING write commits; do not bundle with map registration.

name: JobRunnerStartupStoreError
trigger: At a raised deployment-detail/DISPATCHED/RUNNING store call, before entering runner failure cleanup.

name: ServerEngineStartupError
trigger: At the ordinary server-start returned/raised-error boundary before successful spawn.

name: JobRunnerFailureRemove
trigger: Inside runner exception-cleanup lock after conditional running-job removal and pending-outcome pop.

name: JobRunnerFailureStop
note: Stop is sent only when server run_processes contains the job; it does not reclaim reservations.
trigger: After the blocking failure stop returns, before FAILED_TO_RUN metadata; client stop sends have their own earlier event.

name: JobRunnerFailureStatus
note: Failure-branch store failure is TV-2 first, not injected here.
trigger: After successful FAILED_TO_RUN/status-detail store updates, before the JOB_ABORTED event.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerJobAbortedOnStartFailure
trigger: Inside scheduler event lock after JOB_ABORTED removes the exact failed job ID; before runner retries its outer loop.

name: StartJobProcessorAllocate
trigger: Inside RM lock after popping the reservation; immediately retain the returned allocation in a source-side observer ledger.

name: StartJobProcessorRejectToken
note: Fixed missing-token rejection; no fallback allocation and no rollback when allocation never succeeded.
trigger: At allocate_resources missing-token RuntimeError, before processor builds its error reply; no allocation/free event.

name: ListResourceConsumerConsume
trigger: Immediately after the CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES assignment; capture the assigned unit sequence, not a later reread.

name: ClientEngineStartAppCheck
note: Valid fresh start after acknowledged deployment; early-return alternative is preserved separately.
trigger: After actual executor-status and deployed-app checks succeed; before the executor call.

name: ClientEngineStartAppReturnedError
note: CR-1 boundary: cannot be reached by the selected successful-deploy START chain. No arbitrary deletion fault added; returned error does not free allocation.
trigger: At the missing app-root early return, with unchanged ownership; only if a supported occurrence is established (CR-1).

name: JobExecutorRegisterPendingHandle
trigger: Inside executor.lock immediately after the pending-handle map entry and STARTING status are installed.

name: JobExecutorPrepareException
note: Ordinary preparation/metadata I/O exception before spawn; no fabricated invalid input.
trigger: At an ordinary consume/preparation/metadata I/O exception before spawn; retain allocated payload for processor rollback.

name: ProcessJobLauncherSnapshotEnvironment
trigger: Immediately after new_env = os.environ.copy(); capture new_env CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES before command preparation/spawn.

name: ProcessJobLauncherSpawn
trigger: Immediately after spawn_process succeeds and returns its adapter; capture actual child PID and the passed environment snapshot.

name: ProcessJobLauncherSpawnException
note: Failure before a returned live handle; post-spawn handle-constructor failure is outside this slice.
trigger: At pre-spawn launch exception after executor removes its own pending entry; before propagating to processor rollback.

name: PendingJobHandleAttach

updates.client: [client EXCEPT ![s][t].pc = IF client[s][t].pendingAbort THEN "attachedAbort" ELSE "attached", ![s][t].handle = "attached", ![s][t].attached = TRUE]

trigger: Inside pending_handle._lock after assigning _job_handle and reading the retained abort flag.

name: JobExecutorApplyPendingAbort
trigger: After replaying pending abort against the attached handle, before AFTER_JOB_LAUNCH dispatch.

name: JobExecutorAfterJobLaunchEvent
note: Real event dispatch catches ordinary handler exceptions; no exceptional rollback edge from such handlers.
trigger: After real fire_event(AFTER_JOB_LAUNCH) returns; ordinary handler exceptions remain swallowed, then waiter construction follows.

name: JobExecutorInstallCleanupWaiter
trigger: At successful cleanup-thread start, recording the exact resource payload/handle passed to that waiter.

name: JobExecutorWaiterInstallationException
note: Ordinary Thread construction/start exception before waiter execution. Live attached handle is retained; no invented double-free thread.
trigger: At Thread construction/start exception before any waiter execution; capture retained live handle and propagated exception.

name: StartJobProcessorRollback
note: Rollback calls free(payload) regardless of child liveness or handle ownership. No fictitious token guard on free.
trigger: Inside RM lock after free_resources(payload) appends units; record child/handle independently and the actual free-call count.

name: StartJobProcessorReplySuccess
trigger: After ClientEngine.start_app returns and processor builds the non-error reply, before transport delivery.

name: JobExecutorNotifyStarted
trigger: Immediately after the STARTED assignment in executor.notify_job_status for an existing handle.

name: JobExecutorNotifyStopped
trigger: Immediately after the STOPPED assignment; do not infer process exit or free resources.

name: ClientChildExit
note: Ordinary completion or response to a stop; no guaranteed success under a permanently non-terminating process.
trigger: At observed ordinary OS process exit, retaining PID/handle identity; independently of logical STOPPED and later waiter return.

name: ClientChildFailure
note: Abstract reportable ordinary process failure; generic teardown RC classifications are not expanded.
trigger: At observed reportable OS failure/exit classification, retaining the same owned PID identity.

name: JobExecutorWaitChildExit
trigger: Immediately after job_handle.wait returns and exit code/status are obtained, before attempting terminal reporting.

name: JobExecutorReportOutcome
trigger: After the exact job/site outcome request is enqueued, before waiting for report return.

name: JobExecutorOutcomeReportReturned
note: Reply success or already consumed/lost request followed by return; ReportTimeout covers still-in-flight requests.
trigger: After the reporting call returns normally, before resource free; capture report outcome and transport completion.

name: JobExecutorOutcomeReportException
note: Report exception/timeout is caught; it never bypasses normal resource release.
trigger: At caught reporting exception/timeout, before continuing to the unconditional allocated_resource free block.

name: JobExecutorFreeAfterExit
note: Uses retained payload; deliberately no allocated/token test that would conceal repeated free.
trigger: Inside RM lock after the waiter free call, before executor map removal.

name: JobExecutorRemoveProcess
trigger: Inside executor lock after run_processes.pop(job_id,None), before site-local completion dispatch.

name: JobExecutorJobCompletedEvent
note: Site-local completion event does not call the server scheduler. Explicit job identity is preserved.
trigger: After the site-local JOB_COMPLETED event dispatch returns; it is not a server scheduler event.

name: ClientEngineAbortApp
note: At executor abort ownership update under lock, or ClientEngine no-op early return; termination and wait completion are separate.
trigger: Under executor.lock after setting abort_requested and capturing handle/status, before graceful wait; or at the ClientEngine no-op early return.

name: ClientEngineHeartbeatAbort
note: At executor abort ownership update under lock, or ClientEngine no-op early return; termination and wait completion are separate.
trigger: At the same executor abort boundary for a matching heartbeat-cleanup command; retain heartbeat origin.

name: JobExecutorTerminateAfterGrace
note: 10s bounded graceful wait before terminate; physical process exit remains separate.
trigger: After the 10-second teardown grace and terminate request on the retained attached handle; process exit is another event.

name: FederatedServerHeartbeatCleanup
note: Outcome-map key protects normally completing jobs even when pending set is empty. Repeated heartbeat requests never free resources. Normal periodic response; not an injected, exhaustible fault.
trigger: After _sync_client_jobs derives a job absent from protected server registry/outcome keys, at the heartbeat abort reply boundary.

name: ServerEngineReceiveOutcome
note: Idempotent discard for exact job/site. Receiver authentication and reporter classification are boundary assumptions.
trigger: Inside runner.lock after resolve_client_outcome discards the exact reporting site from the exact job.

name: ServerEngineReceiveFailureOutcome

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![t[1]].pending = IF jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running THEN {} ELSE @ \ {s}, ![t[1]].outcomeKey = IF jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running THEN FALSE ELSE @, ![t[1]].serverFailed = @ \/ jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running, ![t[1]].serverAborted = IF jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running THEN FALSE ELSE @, ![t[1]].serverStop = @ \/ jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered]

note: Authoritative failure bypasses the outcome barrier. Late failure after final removal does not resurrect a job.
trigger: After accepted authoritative failure updates outcome/exception bookkeeping and sends stop; later unknown jobs must not be reactivated.

name: ServerChildExit
trigger: At observed normal server-child OS exit, before wait_for_complete removes the engine map entry.

name: ServerChildFailure
trigger: At observed reportable server-child failure; retain authoritative exception classification.

name: ServerEngineObserveExit
note: Includes finite <=2s UPDATE_RUN_STATUS grace; process already exited.
trigger: Inside server engine lock after wait_for_complete pops the registry entry following wait and status-update grace.

name: ServerEngineTerminateAfterGrace
note: The full 10-second grace branch. Separate early-exit and command-error branches retain their actual deadlines; physical OS exit is independent. Multiple supported abort workers may repeat termination; serverTerminated records occurrence and is not a production guard.
trigger: After the full max_wait=10 cleanup interval and captured-handle termination; early registry removal and zero grace use separate actions.

name: ServerEngineRemoveAfterTerminate
note: CR-2 boundary retained. No injected permanently ineffective SIGKILL or process-count invariant. The final pop(job_id,None) may be a no-op after the exit waiter removed it.
trigger: Inside engine lock immediately after unconditional run_processes.pop following terminate attempt.

name: JobCommandAbortRead
trigger: Immediately after get_job/status read in abort_job, before selecting/performing the store or stop branch.

name: JobCommandAbortPreRunWrite
trigger: Immediately after persistent FINISHED_ABORTED store, before appending CLI success.

name: JobCommandAbortPreRunAcknowledge
note: Acknowledges the saved branch, without rereading status or sending process stop.
trigger: After appending the successful pre-run abort response; retain the saved branch and actual current stored status.

name: JobCommandAbortAlreadyTerminal
trigger: At successful already-terminal CLI response from the saved status branch.

name: JobCommandAbortRunning
trigger: After the blocking running-job stop returns, before mark_run_aborted; client stop sends have their own earlier event.

name: JobRunnerMarkAborted
note: Only an existing running_jobs entry receives run_aborted; missing entry returns an error.
trigger: After inspecting running_jobs and conditionally setting job.run_aborted, before returning success/error.

name: JobRunnerSelectCompletion

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![j].completion = IF jobs[j].pending # {} /\ ~jobs[j].runAborted /\ ~(jobs[j].serverFailed /\ ~jobs[j].serverAborted) THEN "outcomeWait" ELSE "classify", ![j].pending = IF (jobs[j].serverFailed /\ ~jobs[j].serverAborted) THEN {} ELSE @, ![j].outcomeKey = IF (jobs[j].serverFailed /\ ~jobs[j].serverAborted) THEN FALSE ELSE @]

trigger: After reading the job reference and server-map absence, and checking/creating outcome wait state under actual locks.

name: JobRunnerOutcomesResolved
trigger: At the next completion scan when pending is empty or abort/authoritative failure bypasses its wait.

name: JobRunnerOutcomeGraceExpired
note: Crossing the real OutcomeGrace (900s) deadline. No inference that clients have exited.
trigger: At the pending.clear timeout branch, with measured elapsed time since that job outcome deadline was first established.

name: JobRunnerClassifyCompletion

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![j].finishStatus = IF jobs[j].runAborted \/ jobs[j].serverAborted THEN "ABORTED" ELSE IF jobs[j].serverFailed THEN "FAILED" ELSE "COMPLETED", ![j].completion = "archive"]
updates.network: network \cup (IF jobs[j].serverFailed THEN {Msg("Stop",s,<<j,scheduler.issued[j]>>) : s \in jobs[j].deployed} ELSE {})

note: Completion retains a saved reference/status; failure requests client stop independently.
trigger: After saving _FinishedJobState.status and sending failure cleanup as needed, before archival.

name: JobRunnerArchiveSuccess
trigger: After _save_workspace succeeds and workspace_archival_complete is set, before terminal store.

name: JobRunnerArchiveException
note: Retry yields to other jobs; contents omitted, error grace retained.
trigger: At archival exception inside its grace window, before continuing to another job.

name: JobRunnerRetryArchive
trigger: At a later completion scan re-entering _save_workspace for the same saved finished state.

name: JobRunnerArchiveGraceExpired
note: An archive call fails at/after the 60s grace. Reactive completion of prior error, not a newly injected independent fault.
trigger: At an archival error on/after grace, after marking archival processing complete and before terminal store.

name: JobRunnerPublishTerminal
trigger: Immediately after terminal set_status commits, before taking runner lock for deletion.

name: JobRunnerTerminalStoreException
note: Caught store error retries; finite injected errors do not kill completion service.
trigger: At caught terminal set_status failure, before continue/retry; do not remove runner/scheduler entries.

name: JobRunnerRemoveCompleted

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![j].running = FALSE, ![j].pending = {}, ![j].outcomeKey = FALSE, ![j].completedRemoved = TRUE, ![j].completion = IF jobs[j].finishStatus = "ABORTED" THEN "abortedEvent" ELSE "completedEvent"]

note: TV-3 missing-key race is not silently repaired: if running was removed by failure path this action is disabled; see PendingCompletionRemoval structural diagnostic, not a service-death model.
trigger: Inside runner lock after del running_jobs and completion/outcome bookkeeping pops, before lifecycle events.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerJobAbortedOnCompletion
note: ABORTED then COMPLETED are two supported notifications for the same job.
trigger: Inside scheduler.handle_event lock after the ABORTED event removes the exact job membership.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerJobCompleted
trigger: Inside scheduler.handle_event lock after the subsequent COMPLETED removal; duplicate removal is a no-op.

name: TransportLoseMessage
note: Ordinary request/reply loss, no forgery. Tokens and late messages are never reassociated.
trigger: At a controlled ordinary transport drop of a concrete in-flight envelope; record its exact operation/job/site/attempt.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerPersistFailed
note: Deferred end-of-pass failed-job metadata write; successful store boundary.
trigger: At deferred refresh_meta for one failed job after candidate scan returns; before moving to the next failed job.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerPersistBlocked
note: Deferred blocked-job metadata/status processing; successful store boundary.
trigger: At deferred refresh_meta/set_status for one blocked job, after all failed jobs are processed.

name: DefaultJobSchedulerReturnPass
trigger: At schedule_job return after all deferred metadata work, before runner performs its next status check.

name: JobRunnerMissingPendingOutcomes
note: Reactive KeyError path if authoritative failure removed the map during startup. Do not counter-bound an existing-state response.
trigger: At the real KeyError when pending-outcome intersection finds the map was removed, before runner exception cleanup.

name: JobCommandAbortRunningSend
note: Actual client stop send; blocking return and server abort are later.
trigger: At the actual supported running-job client stop send, before its blocking wait; server abort/CLI return are separate.

name: JobRunnerFailureSendStop
note: Failure cleanup sends client stops before blocking return.
trigger: At failure cleanup client stop send, before its blocking wait and the subsequent server abort.

name: JobExecutorAbortStarting
note: STARTING branch invokes pending/attached handle termination after ownership flag update.
trigger: After invoking terminate on the pending or attached STARTING handle; retain the actual pending flag/termination request.

name: ServerEngineReceiveAbortedOutcome

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![t[1]].pending = IF jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running THEN {} ELSE @ \ {s}, ![t[1]].outcomeKey = IF jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running THEN FALSE ELSE @, ![t[1]].serverFailed = @ \/ jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running, ![t[1]].serverAborted = IF (jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered \/ jobs[t[1]].running) /\ ~jobs[t[1]].serverFailed THEN TRUE ELSE @, ![t[1]].serverStop = @ \/ jobs[t[1]].serverRegistered]

note: Accepted ABORTED code sets an exception classification only for an active job and does not overwrite an existing stronger code.
trigger: After accepted ABORTED report processing; capture actual exception classification with stronger-code precedence and cleanup requests.

name: ServerEngineIgnoreOutcome
note: An untracked job/site receives an OK acknowledgement without touching status, pending outcomes or stop state; one terminal report per site/attempt in this slice.
trigger: At the actual receiver early return for a non-pending job/site, before its OK acknowledgement; capture code and exact job/site.

name: ServerEngineResolveMissingOutcome

updates.jobs: [jobs EXCEPT ![t[1]].pending = IF jobs[t[1]].running /\ ~jobs[t[1]].serverFailed THEN {} ELSE @ \ {s}, ![t[1]].outcomeKey = IF jobs[t[1]].running /\ ~jobs[t[1]].serverFailed THEN FALSE ELSE @, ![t[1]].serverFailed = @ \/ jobs[t[1]].running, ![t[1]].serverAborted = IF jobs[t[1]].running /\ ~jobs[t[1]].serverFailed THEN FALSE ELSE @]

note: Heartbeat observes the job absent at this site after server registry removal. It resolves the pending site without an Outcome envelope; active running-map membership gates fail_run. Delayed heartbeat snapshots remain an explicit projection boundary.
trigger: At heartbeat-origin resolve_client_outcome under runner lock, using the actual missing-job observation, pending map and exception outcome.

name: JobExecutorClassifyAbortedExit
note: Returned ABORTED code after a supported stop; independent of physical exit observation.
trigger: At get_return_code classification after physical exit, when the observed returned code is ABORTED and the executor's abort-request flag is set.

name: ServerEngineTerminateAfterExit
note: The graceful loop observes the registry entry already removed and terminates the captured handle without requiring ten seconds. Multiple supported abort workers may repeat termination; serverTerminated records occurrence and is not a production guard.
trigger: After the cleanup loop observed no registry entry and terminated the captured handle; capture the actual loop local and elapsed time.

name: ServerEngineTerminateAfterAbortCommandError
note: Ordinary abort-command exception selects max_wait=0; no claim that a termination request proves process exit. Multiple supported abort workers may repeat termination; serverTerminated records occurrence and is not a production guard.
trigger: After a zero-grace cleanup selected by abort command exception terminates the captured handle; capture max_wait=0.
